account: ProRail, the Dutch rail infrastructure manager, said in a press release of 31 January 2026 that AI software in its smart cameras flags unwanted situations to staff in its Smart Monitoring Room. Those staff alert the rail control room when needed. ProRail also cites research that it says shows that suicides on the track fall 45 percent at locations with both physical measures and cameras. It does not name the study or separate the AI cameras. SpoorPro.nl reported on 2 February 2026 that ProRail is replacing 288 lineside cameras in 2026 with new “smart” cameras. ProRail is also testing drones that fly autonomously and analyze images. SpoorPro quotes ProRail as saying that these forms of camera surveillance help it see and prevent incidents sooner, making the track safer with fewer disruptions and delays. The article's photo caption says that the AI cameras' images are monitored 24/7. The rest of the text is behind a paywall. SpoorPro reported on 3 March 2026 that ProRail is bringing the 7,000 security cameras it manages into one Genetec platform. It is monitored from ProRail's Smart Monitoring Room. Genetec Mission Control filters and analyzes alerts and forwards relevant images to an operator with suggested actions. Video analysis is used among other things to flag spoorlopers (people on the track). In that case the train dispatcher can warn drivers. The article quotes ProRail project lead Kristian Ruiter and Genetec's Bob van Keulen. On 10 September 2026 Genetec, the platform vendor, published a customer story titled “From incident to response in under a minute at ProRail”. No source gives a detection count, a stopped train or a trespass reduction attributable to the analytics. No cited source identifies a trespass-detection trial of the International Union of Railways (UIC).

The trespasser-flagging function is described by Genetec, the platform vendor. Whether the analytics changed any outcome is not reported. The full 2 February 2026 article is paywalled.

fields.headline: ProRail uses Genetec analytics on 7,000 cameras to flag trespass
fields.title: ProRail replaces 288 lineside cameras with AI “smart cameras” in 2026 and uses Genetec video analytics across 7,000 cameras to flag trespassers to train dispatchers

provenance.basis: SHA-256 of the public case, its assessments, and its displayed answers and notes, excluding its own identifier and the derived coverage summary.

value.role: SHA-256 of the complete public case and its assessments

fields.account: ProRail, the Dutch rail infrastructure manager, said in a press release of 31 January 2026 that AI software in its smart cameras flags unwanted situations to staff in its Smart Monitoring Room. Those staff alert the rail control room when needed. ProRail also cites research that it says shows that suicides on the track fall 45 percent at locations with both physical measures and cameras. It does not name the study or separate the AI cameras. SpoorPro.nl reported on 2 February 2026 that ProRail is replacing 288 lineside cameras in 2026 with new “smart” cameras. ProRail is also testing drones that fly autonomously and analyze images. SpoorPro quotes ProRail as saying that these forms of camera surveillance help it see and prevent incidents sooner, making the track safer with fewer disruptions and delays. The article's photo caption says that the AI cameras' images are monitored 24/7. The rest of the text is behind a paywall. SpoorPro reported on 3 March 2026 that ProRail is bringing the 7,000 security cameras it manages into one Genetec platform. It is monitored from ProRail's Smart Monitoring Room. Genetec Mission Control filters and analyzes alerts and forwards relevant images to an operator with suggested actions. Video analysis is used among other things to flag spoorlopers (people on the track). In that case the train dispatcher can warn drivers. The article quotes ProRail project lead Kristian Ruiter and Genetec's Bob van Keulen. On 10 September 2026 Genetec, the platform vendor, published a customer story titled “From incident to response in under a minute at ProRail”. No source gives a detection count, a stopped train or a trespass reduction attributable to the analytics. No cited source identifies a trespass-detection trial of the International Union of Railways (UIC).

must_hold: A dispatcher able to warn drivers once a trespasser is flagged
Privacy masking and blurring applied to passenger images, as the article states ProRail does
produced_by: Thousands of lineside and station security cameras brought into one Genetec video-management platform
Operators in ProRail's Smart Monitoring Room receiving filtered alerts with suggested actions
Video analytics configured to flag people on the track

purpose: Camera upgrades and video analytics intended to detect incidents such as trespassers sooner so that dispatchers can warn drivers. No detection event is documented.

ratings.reason: ProRail says the cameras help it see and prevent incidents sooner. No incident, detection count or delay figure is published.
Fewer trespass incidents and disruptions are the stated aim. No before-and-after data are given.
